name: uniQure N.V.

profile.description: uniQure N.V. is a gene therapy company focused on transformative single-administration therapies for severe genetic diseases. Lead commercial product HEMGENIX is the only FDA-approved AAV gene therapy for hemophilia B, with 75+ patients treated across 8 countries. Lead pipeline candidate AMT-130 for Huntington's disease received FDA agreement on accelerated approval pathway in June 2026, with BLA submission planned Q3 2026. AMT-191 for Fabry disease is also in development. Headquartered in Amsterdam, Netherlands with operations in Lexington, Massachusetts.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): HEMGENIX for hemophilia B is the only FDA-approved AAV gene therapy for the indication, with five-year HOPE-B data confirming long-term durability — mean factor IX activity ~36.1% and ~90% reduction in bleeding rate [1]. Over 75 patients treated across 8 countries validates real-world execution. AMT-130 achieved positive Phase I/II topline results for Huntington's disease with statistically significant slowing of disease progression [2]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI-powered products or quantified AI-driven operational savings reported. Market Share (2/2): Category creator and leader in hemophilia B gene therapy with the only approved AAV-based treatment, defining the treatment paradigm [1]. AMT-130 would be the first-ever gene therapy for Huntington's disease if approved, creating a new therapeutic category [2]. Product Pipeline (2/2): AMT-130 BLA submission planned Q3 2026 with FDA agreement on accelerated approval pathway based on three-year data; AMT-191 for Fabry disease provides additional pipeline visibility; UK MAA submission targeted Q3 2026 [2]. R&D Intensity (1/1): R&D spending of $29.2M in Q1 2026 on $3.6M revenue — R&D intensity vastly exceeds biotech industry averages [3].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): uniQure's purpose — 'delivering on the promise of gene therapy, a single treatment with curative results' — is specific, intentional, and connects gene therapy development to fundamentally changing patient lives for devastating genetic diseases [1]. This differentiates clearly from generic pharma purpose statements and reflects genuine scientific conviction. Community Impact (1/2): Patient advocacy engagement through hemophilia community support programs and partnerships with Huntington's disease patient organizations. No specific dollar amounts for community investment reported. Employee Retention (0/2): The company has grown to approximately 300 employees with SG&A rising from $10.9M to $20.1M in Q1 2026 due to staffing increases [3]. CEO Matt Kapusta has served since ~2016 (joined as CFO in 2015), providing leadership stability after a previous CEO departed after 9 months. No specific retention or tenure data available. Insider Buying (0/2): Net insider selling in 2026 — Chief Medical Officer Walid Abi-Saab sold 1,434 shares and Kylie O'Keefe sold ~16K shares (13% of direct holdings); no significant insider buying identified [4].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics. uniQure remains a pre-profitability biotech with Q1 2026 revenue of $3.6M (up 127% from $1.6M Q1 2025) against a $53.5M net loss [3]. Cash position strengthened to approximately $811M after a $225M public offering in June/July 2026, extending runway into H2 2029 [3][4]. D/E of 269.8% is elevated, driven by accumulated deficit and convertible debt relative to depleted equity base. ROE of -207.1% reflects the deeply unprofitable pre-commercial stage. Revenue growth of 127% YoY scores well but is from a minimal $1.6M base. Forward P/E and PEG are incalculable with negative earnings. Liquidity floor cleared at $42 x ~2M avg daily volume = ~$84M daily [4].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Gene therapy development and manufacturing involves highly regulated biological processes — manufacturing AAV vectors requires specialized GMP facilities, in vivo gene delivery requires neurosurgical procedures (intrathecal injection for AMT-130), and FDA regulatory pathways involve years of clinical data that AI cannot shortcut [1][2]. The physical, biological, and regulatory moats create strong structural protection. However, AI is accelerating drug discovery broadly, potentially enabling competitors to develop rival gene therapies faster. AI Opportunity (0/1): uniQure does not generate quantifiable revenue from AI-related products or services. While AI tools may be used in research workflows, no specific AI-driven revenue contribution has been reported.

infinite_game.summary: uniQure demonstrates genuine purpose through its commitment to curative gene therapies for devastating genetic diseases — a Just Cause that transcends quarterly results. The company has invested for over a decade in gene therapy development before generating meaningful revenue, showing patience and conviction. However, the small organizational size, CEO instability history, and single-product commercial stage limit the depth of infinite game evidence. The FDA pathway agreement for AMT-130 validates the long-term scientific bet [2].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): The vision of curing genetic diseases through one-time gene therapies is a genuine Just Cause — it describes a future where patients with Huntington's, hemophilia B, and Fabry disease are cured rather than managed chronically [1]. HEMGENIX's real-world outcomes (75+ patients, 90% bleeding reduction over 5 years) validate that this is more than marketing. The cause clearly connects to something bigger than revenue. However, the company has not yet proven this purpose through decades of consistent execution — it remains early-stage validation.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): CEO Matt Kapusta has provided stable leadership since ~2016 after a previous CEO departed after just 9 months, restoring continuity [1]. The growing team (~300 employees) includes specialized gene therapy scientists and manufacturing experts with deep domain expertise. SG&A staffing increases in Q1 2026 suggest active team building for AMT-130 commercialization [3]. However, the earlier CEO turnover and small organizational size mean trust evidence is limited.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): uniQure operates in a competitive gene therapy landscape alongside BioMarin, Spark Therapeutics/Roche, and emerging competitors. Management acknowledges competitive dynamics and uses them to sharpen clinical and manufacturing strategies. The company's differentiated AAV platform approach reflects competitive awareness without destructive competitive language.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): uniQure has expanded its gene therapy platform from hemophilia B to Huntington's disease (CNS) and Fabry disease, showing willingness to extend technology into new therapeutic areas with different delivery challenges [1][2]. The pivot from liver-directed to CNS-directed gene therapy represents meaningful scientific and operational adaptation. However, these are extensions of the same AAV platform rather than transformative reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): uniQure has invested over a decade and hundreds of millions of dollars in gene therapy development before generating meaningful revenue, maintaining scientific conviction through multiple market cycles and investor skepticism [1]. The company navigated FDA misalignment on AMT-130's approval pathway in November 2025 and persisted to restore alignment in June 2026, demonstrating regulatory tenacity [2]. The $225M equity raise at higher prices shows willingness to dilute for long-term capability.

investment_thesis: uniQure sits at a pivotal inflection point: on June 17, 2026, the FDA agreed that three-year Phase I/II data from AMT-130 would support a BLA seeking accelerated approval for Huntington's disease, with submission planned Q3 2026 [2]. AMT-130 demonstrated statistically significant slowing of disease progression versus external controls and holds both Breakthrough Therapy and RMAT designations. If approved, AMT-130 would be the first-ever gene therapy for Huntington's disease — addressing a devastating neurodegenerative condition with no disease-modifying treatments available today. The company's cash position of approximately $811M (post-$225M offering) provides runway into H2 2029, de-risking the regulatory and commercialization timeline [3][4]. HEMGENIX continues real-world validation with 75+ hemophilia B patients treated across 8 countries [1].
thesis_continued: The bear case remains formidable despite the regulatory milestone. HEMGENIX revenue of just $3.6M in Q1 2026 (up from $1.6M) demonstrates that even an approved gene therapy faces slow commercial adoption due to pricing ($3.5M per treatment), payer resistance, and small addressable patient populations [3]. The $199M FY2025 net loss and D/E of 270% underscore continued capital market dependence. AMT-130 faces significant execution risk: the FDA agreed on accelerated approval but requires a confirmatory study with concurrent control (not sham surgery), adding time and cost [2]. Huntington's disease has historically been extremely difficult therapeutically. At $42/share ($2.8B market cap), much of the AMT-130 de-risking is already priced in, and any regulatory or clinical setback would severely compress the stock given no near-term path to profitability [4].
key_catalysts: AMT-130 BLA submission to FDA in Q3 2026 for accelerated approval in Huntington's disease, with Breakthrough Therapy and RMAT designations potentially accelerating review timeline [2]
Four-year AMT-130 durability data readout in Q3 2026 and UK MAA submission providing additional regulatory milestones and de-risking events [2]
HEMGENIX commercial acceleration through expanded geographic access and growing physician adoption, with 75+ patients treated as proof-of-concept for gene therapy commercialization [1]
key_risks: AMT-130 regulatory risk — FDA requires a confirmatory study with concurrent standard-of-care control rather than sham surgery, adding years and significant cost to the approval pathway [2]
Gene therapy commercialization challenge — HEMGENIX generates only $3.6M/quarter despite FDA approval, highlighting severe pricing, payer, and adoption headwinds for $3.5M one-time treatments [3]

Capital markets dependence — with $199M annual net loss and no path to near-term profitability, the $811M cash position (H2 2029 runway) may still require additional dilutive financing if AMT-130 commercialization costs exceed expectations [3][4]
